summary: Iteration-2 e2e test of Cortexa (streaming chat, permission engine, themes, wake word, new orb). BACKEND: created /app/backend/tests/test_stream_tools.py (13 pytest cases) - SSE event ordering (session -> N deltas -> done), multi-token streaming, transcript persistence via /api/chat/sessions/{id}, 401 on unauthenticated stream, risky-message tool_request emission (write_file/delete_file, risk=CONFIRM, status=pending, uuid id, emitted before done), approve -> executed + simulated result, double-resolve -> 400, bogus id -> 404, deny -> denied + 'Cancelled by user', /api/activity contains 'Tool executed: write_file' and 'Tool denied: delete_file', plus regression on /auth/me, /agents, /tasks CRUD (POST/GET/PATCH), /system/telemetry, non-streaming /chat. Result 13/13 PASSED (100%). FRONTEND (Playwright, 1920x1080, real Claude calls): login -> home; new CortexaCore orb renders (data-testid cortexa-core, 1 SVG + 54 ring/waveform nodes, royal blue, data-theme=royal); command-bar message streamed token-by-token (bubble grew over time, .stream-caret visible during stream, final reply 89 chars); 'Write a file called notes.txt with hello world' -> perm-card-write_file appeared after streamed reply, Confirm & Run -> perm-result 'File written successfully - 1 file changed (simulated)'; 'Delete the file temp.log' -> perm-card-delete_file -> Cancel -> 'Cancelled by user - nothing was executed.'; Settings>Appearance shows all 4 swatches, clicking Violet flips data-theme=violet and --accent-1 #4a6cff -> #8b5cf6, persists across reload (localStorage cortexa_theme), active class/check/border track selection correctly (verified for violet + crimson), reverted to royal; Settings>Voice - this headless Chromium DOES expose SpeechRecognition, so the toggle was ENABLED (not disabled): checking it showed wake-status-chip in Settings AND wake-indicator in TitleBar, unchecking removed the indicator (no wake-unsupported warning path exercised); Agents/Memory/Tasks/System/History all render with 0 error elements and no cyan (only intentional emerald rgb(52,211,153) status green remains); quick action 'System Info' triggered a streamed 894-char reply. Zero console/page errors in all runs. Frontend 100% of requested flows passed.

minor.issue: Permission gate is a narrow regex requiring an explicit file/folder/script noun, so many risky phrasings bypass it entirely (verified by importing server.detect_tool_request): 'Delete temp.log' -> None, 'rm -rf /important' -> None, 'install VS Code' -> None, 'run npm build' -> None, 'format my C drive' -> None, 'erase all my photos' -> None. The LLM then answers freely with no confirm card, defeating the feature's promise.
If the LLM stream throws before any delta (full == ''), the user's own turn is never persisted to chat_messages and no activity entry is logged - the message is silently lost from history.
Mid-stream failures are emitted as an SSE 'error' event inside a 200 response, so proxies/clients cannot detect failure by status. Also the tool_request row is inserted even when the LLM failed.

UI advertises three risk tiers (LOW auto-exec / CONFIRM / BLOCKED never run) but the backend only implements CONFIRM; there is no BLOCKED list, so e.g. 'format disk' phrasing is neither blocked nor gated.

minor.issue: PATCH /api/tasks/{id} 500 on unknown id; register/me email-casing mismatch; DELETE /agents|/memory always {ok:true}; /api/chat replays history with one LLM call per stored user turn.

ui_bugs.issue: Assistant replies render raw markdown as literal text ('**notes.txt**', '`write_file`', '--' separators) because the bubble prints m.text directly. Very visible on every reply - needs a markdown renderer or a system-prompt instruction to reply in plain text.
catch (_) only clears busy - a failed resolve (e.g. 400 already-resolved after a reload, or network error) leaves the permission card silently stuck in pending with no error surfaced to the user.
data-testid uses the array index (bubble-bot-${i}), so indices shift whenever a permission card is inserted - unstable for automation. Prefer a stable id-based testid.
onDone() fires twice per stream (once on the 'done' event, again after the reader loop exits). Currently harmless/idempotent but will double-fire any future side effect.
If the stream fails after partial text, the bubble just stops (streaming=false) with no error affordance and no retry - the user cannot tell the reply was truncated.

issues: Content panel is ~850px tall while Appearance/Voice/About render only 2-4 rows of content - ~70% dead space on a 1080p viewport.
Left tab labels still use var(--text-dim) on near-black (low contrast, likely below WCAG AA) - reported in iteration 1, unchanged.
Empty chat panel leaves a very large blank area between the last bubble and the command bar while waiting for a permission card / long reply; consider top-aligned compact layout or a placeholder.

design_issues.screen: Right panel - Recent Activity / Your Agents
issues: Iteration-1 findings unchanged: agent name+role wrap to 2-3 lines making rows uneven; activity fallback still worth an empty state.

action_items: Broaden / rethink the risky-action classifier: 'Delete temp.log', 'rm -rf ...', 'install VS Code', 'run npm build', 'format my C drive', 'erase all my photos' all bypass the permission card today. Consider LLM tool-calling or a much wider pattern set + a BLOCKED tier so the Settings>Permissions copy is truthful.
Render markdown in bot bubbles (or instruct the model to reply in plain text) - every reply currently shows literal ** and backticks.
Surface an error state in resolveTool's catch block so a failed confirm/cancel does not leave the permission card stuck pending.
Persist the user's turn in /api/chat/stream even when the LLM stream errors before the first delta; skip inserting the tool_request row on stream failure.
Make chat bubble data-testids id-based instead of index-based.
Fire onDone only once in lib/stream.js.

Still open from iteration 1: PATCH /api/tasks/{id} 500 on unknown id, register/me email casing, delete endpoints returning ok:true for no-ops, /api/chat history replay cost, Settings tab-label contrast.
critical_code_review_comments: detect_tool_request is a 5-regex allowlist of phrasings; a permission/safety gate built on keyword matching fails open (no card => LLM answers as if allowed). Prefer real tool-calling with a server-side risk table.
chat_stream inserts the tool_requests document unconditionally after the stream, even when the generator emitted an 'error' event, creating pending tool rows for failed turns.
streaming errors are reported with HTTP 200 + an in-body SSE error event; frontend onError only replaces the bubble when text is empty, so partial failures are invisible.
Home.jsx sendMessage/resolveTool swallow all errors (catch (_)) - no user-visible failure path, same anti-pattern flagged in RightPanel.jsx last iteration.
Settings>Permissions text describes LOW/CONFIRM/BLOCKED tiers that do not exist in the backend - documentation/implementation drift.

rca_of_the_issue: Main functional gap: the permission engine's risk detection lives in RISKY_PATTERNS (server.py ~line 440), five regexes each requiring BOTH a verb and an explicit noun such as file/folder/script/app within 40 chars. Reproduction: `python -c "import server; print(server.detect_tool_request('Delete temp.log'))"` -> None; same for 'rm -rf /important', 'install VS Code', 'run npm build', 'format my C drive'. Because no tool_request is emitted, the UI shows no confirm card and the LLM answers the risky request unguarded. Mitigation: move classification into model tool-calling (or a substantially broader pattern set incl. bare filenames/extensions and shell verbs) and add an explicit BLOCKED tier to match the Settings>Permissions copy.
